derivation_before: Fix an integer $t$. The recurrence through $t$ is a finite expression DAG with positive exact divisors and logarithm arguments, since every iterate has full support. The algorithm uses mantissa precision $r^2$, exponent bounds $-r,r$, and truncation $N=r$. Uniformly for each endpoint $x$ in a fixed bounded input interval, the evaluator in [F6] uses $s=r+2$ squarings after reducing to $u=x/2^s$. On a fixed bounded neighborhood of $x$, [F7] bounds the initial series error by $C^{r+1}2^{-s(r+1)}/(r+1)!$ for some fixed $Cge1$, and the endpoint rounding error by $O(2^{-r^2})$. The exact intermediate exponentials are uniformly bounded; on a fixed larger bounded interval, squaring is Lipschitz with some fixed constant $A>1$. Thus the total endpoint error after $s$ rounded squarings is at most $A^{r+2}$ times the initial error plus $O(A^{r+2}2^{-r^2})$, which tends to zero. The exact exponential is Lipschitz on that interval, so a shrinking input interval has a shrinking output enclosure. This bound also ensures the rounded intermediates remain in that larger interval for all sufficiently large $r$. Logarithm range reduction on a fixed positive compact interval uses only finitely many bins; its series tails tend to zero, and its endpoint operations are continuous there. Rational input rounding likewise converges by [F7]. Applying these bounds successively to the finite recurrence DAG shows every requested enclosure width tends to zero. All exact positive divisors and logarithm arguments are eventually separated from zero, and the expanding exponent range eventually avoids overflow. The finite maximum forming $G_t$ preserves convergence, so its logarithm enclosure also shrinks to $lngamma_t$. Soundness follows from [F6]. Hence each fixed-$t$ precision loop terminates with the required width.
